The library has **four papers that propose and test a remedy**, all in `library/llm/context/`. A fifth, *Lost in the Middle* itself, tries one prompt change. Each remedy changes a different thing: the model's weights, its attention, its position indices, or the input. I took the facts below from each paper's note and checked them against the context review. I didn't open the PDFs, and no conversion problems are recorded for these papers.

### 1. Change the weights: *Make Your LLM Fully Utilize the Context* (FILM-7B, IN2 training)
- **Assumed cause:** long-context training rarely rewards using a detail far from the question. The data also has a built-in position bias, for example the system message always comes first ([p. 2](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Make%20Your%20LLM%20Fully%20Utilize%20the%20Context.pdf?page=2)).
- **What changes:** fine-tuning on synthetic question-answer pairs. Each context is 4K–32K tokens of shuffled 128-token segments. The answer depends either on one segment, or on two or more segments from one text that may sit far apart ([p. 3](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Make%20Your%20LLM%20Fully%20Utilize%20the%20Context.pdf?page=3)). The base model is Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2, trained for about 300 GPU-days ([p. 4](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Make%20Your%20LLM%20Fully%20Utilize%20the%20Context.pdf?page=4)). Inference is unchanged.
- **Result:** on the authors' own position probes, the average rises from 47.3 to 85.9. The gap between best and worst position falls from 56.2 to 13.9 ([p. 6, Table 1](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Make%20Your%20LLM%20Fully%20Utilize%20the%20Context.pdf?dest=table.1&page=6)). On nine LongBench tasks the average goes from 30.6 to 39.9, almost all of it from question answering. Summarisation barely moves, e.g. GovReport 33.3 → 33.8 ([p. 6–7, Table 2](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Make%20Your%20LLM%20Fully%20Utilize%20the%20Context.pdf?dest=table.2&page=6)).

### 2. Change the attention at inference: *Found in the Middle*
- **Assumed cause:** attention follows a U shape and favours the first and last documents whatever they contain ([p. 1](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Found%20in%20the%20Middle.%20Calibrating%20Positional%20Attention%20Bias%20Improves%20Long%20Context%20Utilization.pdf?page=1)).
- **What changes:** the paper models attention to a document as relevance plus a position bias. It measures the bias as the attention a dummy document gets at each position, and subtracts it ([p. 5, Eq. 3–4](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Found%20in%20the%20Middle.%20Calibrating%20Positional%20Attention%20Bias%20Improves%20Long%20Context%20Utilization.pdf?page=5)). It then rescales each document's attention towards what remains, a relevance estimate ([p. 6, Eq. 5–6](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Found%20in%20the%20Middle.%20Calibrating%20Positional%20Attention%20Bias%20Improves%20Long%20Context%20Utilization.pdf?page=6)). This is applied only to the last 16 of 32 layers ([p. 13, App. B](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Found%20in%20the%20Middle.%20Calibrating%20Positional%20Attention%20Bias%20Improves%20Long%20Context%20Utilization.pdf?page=13)).
- **Cost:** no training, but it needs access to the attention weights and about K extra forward passes for K documents ([p. 9](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Found%20in%20the%20Middle.%20Calibrating%20Positional%20Attention%20Bias%20Improves%20Long%20Context%20Utilization.pdf?page=9)).
- **Result:** with the answer in the middle, accuracy rises 6–15 points on two 7B models. For example, Vicuna on 20-document NaturalQuestions goes from 47.34 to 56.19 ([p. 13, Table 5](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Found%20in%20the%20Middle.%20Calibrating%20Positional%20Attention%20Bias%20Improves%20Long%20Context%20Utilization.pdf?dest=table.5&page=13)). It loses where the model was already strong: with the answer first, that model drops from 71.93 to 66.40 (same table). On SynthWiki, calibration alone also loses to simply reordering the documents (same table). The authors say attention is "not necessarily causal" ([p. 3](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Found%20in%20the%20Middle.%20Calibrating%20Positional%20Attention%20Bias%20Improves%20Long%20Context%20Utilization.pdf?page=3)).

### 3. Change the position indices at inference: *Why Does the Effective Context Length of LLMs Fall Short?* (STRING)
- **Assumed cause:** large distances between tokens are rarely seen in training. In a sequence of length L, distance i occurs L − i times ([p. 3, Eq. 1–2](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Why%20Does%20the%20Effective%20Context%20Length%20of%20LLMs%20Fall%20Short.pdf?page=3)). Failures cluster on evidence far from the question, which at 128K means the *start* of the input, not the middle ([p. 5](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Why%20Does%20the%20Effective%20Context%20Length%20of%20LLMs%20Fall%20Short.pdf?page=5)).
- **What changes:** it drops the largest relative positions and shifts distant tokens onto smaller, well-trained positions. A local window of 128 tokens stays intact, with shift S = L/3 ([p. 6, Eq. 3–4](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Why%20Does%20the%20Effective%20Context%20Length%20of%20LLMs%20Fall%20Short.pdf?page=6)). There is no training. It applies to models with RoPE position encoding and needs open weights.
- **Result:** on the RULER benchmark at 128K, Llama3.1 70B goes from 66.6 to 81.7 and Qwen2 72B from 53.7 to 84.6. Llama3.1 8B gains only 77.0 → 80.0 ([p. 8, Table 2](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Why%20Does%20the%20Effective%20Context%20Length%20of%20LLMs%20Fall%20Short.pdf?dest=table.2&page=8)).

### 4. Change the input: *LongLLMLingua*
- **What changes:** the model stays frozen and can be an API model. Before the call, a small model scores each document by how likely the question is given that document, and keeps the best ones ([p. 3, Eq. 2](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/LongLLMLingua.%20Accelerating%20and%20Enhancing%20LLMs%20in%20Long%20Context%20Scenarios%20via%20Prompt%20Compression.pdf?page=3)). It **reorders** the kept documents with the most relevant first ([p. 4, Eq. 4](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/LongLLMLingua.%20Accelerating%20and%20Enhancing%20LLMs%20in%20Long%20Context%20Scenarios%20via%20Prompt%20Compression.pdf?page=4)), then cuts tokens using the question.
- **Result:** on GPT-3.5-Turbo with 20 documents, the uncompressed prompt scores 75.7 / 57.3 / 54.1 / 55.4 / 63.1 with the answer at position 1 / 5 / 10 / 15 / 20. LongLLMLingua at 4x compression scores 75.0 / 71.8 / 71.2 / 71.2 / 74.7 ([p. 5, Table 1](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/LongLLMLingua.%20Accelerating%20and%20Enhancing%20LLMs%20in%20Long%20Context%20Scenarios%20via%20Prompt%20Compression.pdf?dest=table.1&page=5)). In the ablation, most of the gain comes from the document scoring, not the reordering. Reordering costs a point when the answer is first, 77.2 → 76.2 ([p. 6, Table 3](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/LongLLMLingua.%20Accelerating%20and%20Enhancing%20LLMs%20in%20Long%20Context%20Scenarios%20via%20Prompt%20Compression.pdf?dest=table.3&page=6)).

### A partial fix: *Lost in the Middle* itself
- **Prompt change:** putting the question both before and after the data. On the key–value task every model gets near-perfect accuracy; GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K) goes from a worst case of 45.6% to perfect at 300 pairs. On multi-document question answering it barely changes the curve ([p. 7](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Lost%20in%20the%20Middle.%20How%20Language%20Models%20Use%20Long%20Contexts.pdf?page=7)).
- **Untested suggestion:** rerank so the relevant documents come first, or keep fewer of them ([p. 9](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Lost%20in%20the%20Middle.%20How%20Language%20Models%20Use%20Long%20Contexts.pdf?page=9)).

### How far to trust these
- **Narrow tests:** each remedy rests on one paper, a few open models, and benchmarks the authors chose or built.
- **No head-to-head:** no paper compares two of the remedies on the same model.
- **Older models:** none is tested on current frontier models.

About 20 other papers here mention lost-in-the-middle, e.g. *RECOMP*, *Retrieval meets Long Context*, *MemAgent* and *PersonaMem-v3*. They cite it as motivation or measure it again, but don't propose and test a fix for it.
